title: SXF / AI — Eight-case claim-verification demonstration
protocol: A deliberately constructed editorial before/after audit, NOT a captured chatbot evaluation.
evidenceBasis: Human-reviewed first-party public documents, with a deterministic schema/consistency test.
uncheckedAnswersAre: Purpose-written unsafe example drafts, not raw model outputs or representative samples.
verifiedAnswersAre: Editor-rewritten conclusions anchored to the linked first-party documents.
nonClaims: No ChatGPT or Gemini live calls were recorded.
No model hallucination rate, source-retrieval effect size, error reduction percentage, or statistically generalizable performance claim.
Source meaning is human-reviewed; automated tests check artifact structure and consistency, not scientific truth.

openai-help.name: OpenAI Help Center — Does ChatGPT tell the truth?

nist.name: NIST AI 600-1 — Generative AI Profile, §2.2 Confabulation

cases.question: If ChatGPT sounds completely certain, is the answer definitely true?
cases.unchecked: Yes. A confident tone means the information has been checked.
cases.verified: No. Confidence in wording is not a reliability measure; confirm consequential claims independently.
cases.check: Find OpenAI's warning that models can sound confident even when they are wrong.

cases.question: Does a citation in an AI answer prove the cited article exists?
cases.unchecked: Yes. A formatted journal citation is evidence that the paper exists.
cases.verified: No. A citation can be fabricated. Open the source and verify the title, authors and whether the source supports the claim.
cases.check: Locate OpenAI's explicit examples of fabricated quotes, studies, citations or references.

cases.question: Can searching the web remove every hallucination?
cases.unchecked: Yes. An AI answer with search enabled is guaranteed to be correct.
cases.verified: No. Search can improve verification, but a retrieved page or link is not proof that the generated claim matches that source.
cases.check: Compare the stated benefit of search with the recommendation to verify important information.

cases.question: Can ChatGPT know today's changed rule without accessing a current source?
cases.unchecked: Yes. A fluent answer is enough to confirm the most recent rule.
cases.verified: Not necessarily. Without appropriate current retrieval, a model can miss information that changed after its training data.
cases.check: Check the Help Center's distinction between answers without search and with current search tools.

cases.question: If the AI puts a sentence in quotation marks, is it a real quote?
cases.unchecked: Yes. Quotation marks show it was copied exactly.
cases.verified: No. A quote may be invented or altered; open the original document and match the exact words and context.
cases.check: Review the fabricated-quotation example and verify the wording at the alleged source.

cases.question: What if a question leaves out the year, country or which person?
cases.unchecked: The model should confidently choose one interpretation without mentioning it.
cases.verified: Ask for the missing detail or state the assumption; ambiguous questions can prompt overconfident, misleading answers.
cases.check: Locate the Help Center's caution about overconfident answers to ambiguous questions.

cases.question: When a model hallucinates, does that prove it consciously intended to deceive?
cases.unchecked: Yes. An incorrect answer proves the AI wanted to lie.
cases.verified: No. A false generated response does not establish intention. NIST uses 'confabulation' and describes risks from fluent false statements.
cases.check: Read §2.2 Confabulation and distinguish output-level error from claims about intent.

cases.question: Can evaluation design make unsupported guessing more attractive than saying 'I don't know'?
cases.unchecked: Every model always guesses because every evaluation rewards bluffing.
cases.verified: Some standard accuracy-based evaluations can reward guessing over abstention; this is a research explanation, not a universal claim about every model or test.
cases.check: Read the research summary's qualified claim about common training and evaluation incentives.
